summary: Make Git ancestry the default missing receipt policy for adopters

delivery.outcome: New adopters use Git ancestry to resolve merged ticket directories when the optional terminal-receipt registry is absent, eliminating stale active-ticket projections after ordinary protected merges.
nonGoals: Do not weaken receipt validation or rewrite the append-only terminal receipt registry.
Do not change the explicit status-projection option for adopters that retain it.
Do not infer terminal state from an unmerged ticket branch or from carrier-only changes.

architecture.decision: Change only the managed package default from status-projection to git-ancestry. The resolver already verifies the target ref and rejects carrier-only delivery; existing adopters may retain the conservative policy explicitly.
interfaceChanges: New package adopters receive registry.missingPolicy=git-ancestry by default
architecture.rollback: Restore status-projection in governance/ticket-activity.json and the conservative fixture expectation.

validation.evidence: A missing registry resolves a ticket whose directory is on the target as terminal under the new default, while an explicit status-projection policy remains conservative.
All standard governance and ticket-activity suites pass with the published package projection.
